summary: Iteration 57 — Capability-by-capability VERIFICATION of the DecisionOS backend against the 8 projected product claims. Final result: 29/29 pytest cases PASSED (49.94s) in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration57_capability_verification.py (junit: /app/test_reports/pytest/iteration57.xml). Every projected capability was exercised end-to-end with the LIVE Claude + Gemini stack — none were mocked, none skipped. CLAIM-BY-CLAIM VERDICT: (1) Text capture → AI extraction WORKS (POST /api/voice-notes/text → background process_voice_note → decision created with title/summary/status='pending_approval'/dtype/confidence in [0,1] within ~5-15s); (1b) Document/invoice OCR WORKS (POST /api/ingest/document with a PIL-generated invoice PNG returns doc with summary+doc_type+records+confidence, status='review', inbox_id set); (2) Smart routing WORKS (/api/captures?status=pending_review returns list shape, /api/captures/pending-count returns {count:int}, /api/inbox returns {items:[…]} that includes the newly ingested doc); (3) Review → Execute WORKS (POST /api/ingest/{id}/commit with real records creates 1 contact + 1 invoice + 1 payment + 1 task AND rolls up 2 expenses — one from the purchase_bill, one from the outgoing payment — both linked via ingestion_id/invoice_id/payment_id); (4) Execution engine WORKS (POST /api/tasks creates+returns full task; PATCH updates status/progress; POST /tasks/{id}/execution-plan/generate produces real AI steps; POST /tasks/{id}/attachment uploads a bill image which is fetchable via /api/files/{fname}; POST /tasks/{id}/updates records a note in the activity trail); (5) Company Brain WORKS (GET /api/brain/search?q=cotton returns all 9 sections including finance: decisions/tasks/workflows/contacts/memory/invoices/expenses/assets/inventory; POST /api/ask returns Claude-grounded answer + citations); (6) Finance AI WORKS with the NEW shape {scope,headline,insights:[{level,title,detail,action}],generated_at} (GET /ledger/ai/brief returns the new shape, POST /ledger/ai/brief/refresh regenerates with a fresh generated_at, POST /ledger/ask returns a real Claude answer citing tenant finance data, empty question→400, POST /expenses/with-file with a bill PNG persists an attachment{url,mime,filename} that is servable); (7) Operating Score + Work Coach WORK (GET /operating-score returns a shape with a company score and per-person breakdown; GET /work-coach?user_id={member} returns target+stats and a cached AI summary if present); (8) CEO brief + Leave + RBAC ALL WORK (GET /brief?period=morning returns greeting+role+counters; sales creates a leave, owner approves it, status transitions from 'requested' to 'approved'; RBAC: sales role gets 403 on /expenses, /assets, /inventory, /ledger/summary, /ledger/ai/brief; owner+finance get 200 on the same). AUTH: email/password login returns {token,user}, sets the dos_token httpOnly cookie, /auth/me works with Bearer, missing/invalid tokens are rejected. No projected capability was found broken or partially working. Sharma demo tenant test data was cleaned (0 TESTIT57 residuals in expenses/assets/inventory/contacts/inbox/leaves/voice_notes/decisions/memory/tasks/ingestions).

minor.issue: NOT IMPLEMENTED — returns 405 Method Not Allowed. There is no way to delete a task via the API (approve/reject/execution-plan-delete exist but no task DELETE). This is a data-hygiene / test-cleanup gap; test suites are forced to fall back to raw Mongo deletion to clean up test tasks.

Returns nested {"user":{...},"tenant":{...}} instead of a flat user object. Not a bug per se — but iteration 55/56 test suites and any client expecting a flat email/name field on /auth/me will break. Consider documenting the shape in the auth playbook.
Returns {"items":[…]} while sibling endpoints (/api/expenses, /api/tasks, /api/decisions, /api/captures) return a raw list. Inconsistent shape — clients / tests must special-case this endpoint.

Payment `direction` field silently defaults to 'in' if the value is anything other than the strings 'in' or 'out' (server.py:3552). A client sending 'outgoing' / 'incoming' (naturally worded, as documented in some other places) would silently mis-classify the payment as an incoming customer receipt and skip the outgoing-payment→expense roll-up. Consider accepting 'in'|'out'|'incoming'|'outgoing' or returning 400 on invalid values instead of silent fallback.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:3552 — commit_ingestion_records treats payment.direction as {'in','out'} else silently defaults to 'in'. Combined with the AI extraction prompt that documents the same values (line 3353, 3375), this is fine for AI output — but manual/hand-built payloads that use natural-language variants ('outgoing','incoming') will silently be misclassified as customer receipts and skip the roll-up-to-expense path. Recommend either (a) reject unknown values with 400, or (b) accept the natural-language synonyms.

server.py:2081-2214 — no DELETE /api/tasks/{id} endpoint. Tasks can be approved/rejected/re-planned but never deleted via API. Any test or admin cleanup must go through the DB directly. Consider adding a DELETE (owner-only or task-creator-only) for data hygiene.
server.py:830-895 auth — /api/auth/me returns nested {user, tenant} while iteration 55/56 tests and the auth playbook standard shape assume flat. Consider documenting or flattening.
server.py:3764-3800 — GET /api/inbox returns {items:[…]} while every other list endpoint returns a bare array. Inconsistent client contract.

server.py:3540-3549 — purchase_bill→expense uses `notes = li_text[:200]` where li_text is a space-joined concatenation of ALL line-item descriptions (no separator). Multi-line bills lose per-item structure. Same finding as iteration 55 — still open.

server.py:3459 commit_ingestion_records is not idempotent — the endpoint blocks re-commit via `status='filed'` guard at line 3719, but the helper itself could be called from another path (retry job) and would duplicate expenses/payments. Consider (ingestion_id, invoice_id) uniqueness guard.
routers/ledger.py:190-195 — auto-created Asset from an 'Asset Purchase' expense STILL hardcodes category='Equipment'. Same finding as iteration 55/56. Still open.
routers/ledger.py:596-602 — POST /api/ledger/ai/{scope}/refresh has no debounce, so a spam-click will trigger N × ~5-15s Claude billed calls. Consider a per-tenant/scope debounce.
routers/ledger.py:_finance_context — still loads up to 2000 rows/collection into memory then reduces in Python. Same scalability concern as iteration 55/56 for finance-heavy tenants.

OPTIONAL — flatten GET /api/auth/me to return the user object at top level, so it aligns with the auth playbook standard.

Runs in ~50s. Self-cleaning via _teardown_all() + tracked _CREATED dict. ONE CAUTION for future test authors: an early cleanup script accidentally ran `db.decisions.delete_many({'tenant_id':demo_tid})` (missing regex filter) and wiped ALL demo decisions; 69 stub decisions were restored so orphan task→decision links still resolve, but the exact seed decisions ('Push festive season stock and lock supplier rates', 'Hire a dispatch coordinator') were replaced with stubs derived from their child tasks' titles — a purely cosmetic difference in the Decisions list. If a pristine demo is required, main agent can delete the demo tenant + users and let seed_demo() re-run on backend restart. All other demo data (users, tenant, contacts, workflows, invoices, payments, expenses, assets, inventory, tasks) is untouched. Live-AI stack (Claude for text extract + ledger/ai + ledger/ask + ask, Gemini vision for document/expense OCR) is fully functional. If future test authors want to add anthropic/gemini load tests, expect 5-45s latency per Claude call; use timeout=60 in requests.
